questions.question: Who is considered the highest law officer of the state in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Advocate General**__.

__
 
• The Advocate General of the state is the highest law officer in the state.
 
• He/she is appointed by the Governor of the state.
 
• The Advocate General's duty is to advise the state government on legal matters.
 
• The Advocate General has the right to speak and take part in the proceedings of both houses of the state legislature, but without the right to vote.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Attorney General of India**

 
 
• The Attorney General is the highest law officer in the country.
 
• He/she is appointed by the President of India.
 
• The Attorney General's duty is to give advice to the Government of India on legal matters and perform other legal duties assigned to him/her.
 
• The Attorney General has the right to participate in the proceedings of both houses of Parliament but without the right to vote.
 
 
 
• **Chief Justice of High Court**
 
 
• The Chief Justice is the head of the judiciary in a state.
 
• He/she is appointed by the President of India in consultation with the Chief Justice of India and the Governor of the state.
 
• The Chief Justice's duty is to preside over the high court and ensure the administration of justice in the state.
 
 
 
• **Auditor General**
 
 
• The Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG) is the authority responsible for auditing the accounts of the state and central governments and public sector organizations.
 
• The CAG is appointed by the President of India.
 
• The CAG's duty is to ensure that public funds are used efficiently and for the intended purposes.

questions.question: In India the State election Commissioner is appointed by the _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Governor**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **State Election Commissioner (SEC):-**

 
 
• The role of the State Election Commissioner is primarily defined under Article 243K of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It is a crucial constitutional and administrative figure responsible for conducting and supervising elections within a particular state or union territory in India.
 
• **The State Election Commissioner is usually appointed by the Governor of the state. **
 
• The appointment is made after consultation with the State Government, but it is important that the Commissioner is not under the direct influence of the government to ensure the autonomy of the election process.
 
• The tenure of the State Election Commissioner is usually determined by the Governor, and it may vary from state to state. 
 
 
 
• **Governor**:-
 
 
• Governor is the chief executive head of a state.
 
• He is appointed by the President for a term of 5 years and is subjected to pleasure of the President.
 
• The President may transfer a Governor to another state.
 
• The Constitution does not provide any cases of contingency in regard to Governor for example death of the Governor.
 
• Article 160 states that The President can make such provisions as he thinks fit for the discharge of functions of governor in any contingency.
 
• When the Governor of a state dies in office, anyone designated by the President takes over as acting Governor.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• It is the highest-ranking judicial officer in India.
 
• It serves as the head of the Indian judiciary.
 
 
 
• **President**:-
 
 
• President of a country is typically the ceremonial head of state and holds a position of constitutional importance.
 
• The President is elected by an Electoral College comprising elected members of both houses of Parliament and state legislative assemblies.
 
 
 
• **Chief Minister:-**
 
 
• It is the head of the state government in a particular state or union territory.

__
 
• The tenure of the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) is **6 years or up to the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier.**
 
• The Chief Election Commissioner can be removed from office **only through impeachment by Parliament** for proven misbehavior or incapacity.
 
• The CEC and other Election Commissioners have the same powers, salary, allowances, and other perquisites as are available to a judge of the **Supreme Court of India.**
 
• The concept of an independent Election Commission was introduced to ensure free and fair elections in India, as per the provisions of **Article 324** of the Indian Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Election Commission of India (ECI)**

 
 
• The Election Commission of India is an autonomous constitutional authority responsible for administering election processes in India at both the national and state levels.
 
• The body administers elections to the Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, and State Legislative Assemblies, as well as the offices of the President and Vice President in the country.
 
• The Election Commission operates under the authority of Constitution per Article 324, and subsequently enacted Representation of the People Act.
 
• The commission has the powers to monitor the election process, including the preparation of electoral rolls, ensuring the model code of conduct, and scrutinizing election expenses of candidates.
 
 
 
• **Chief Election Commissioner (CEC)**
 
 
• The Chief Election Commissioner heads the Election Commission of India and oversees the entire electoral process.
 
• Appointed by the President of India, the CEC ensures that the election process is conducted in a free, fair, and impartial manner.
 
• The CEC can only be removed through a process similar to that of a judge of the Supreme Court, which requires a two-thirds majority in Parliament.
 
• The CEC’s role is critical in maintaining the sanctity of the democratic process in India.

questions.question: Which part of the Indian Constitution deals with the Election Commission?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Part XV**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Part XV of the Indian Constitution** deals with elections, which includes provisions related to the Election Commission of India.
 
• It encompasses **Articles 324 to 329**, which provide the framework for the conduct of elections in the country.
 
• Article 324 specifically **vests the power of superintendence, direction, and control of elections** in an independent Election Commission.
 
• The Election Commission is responsible for conducting elections to the Parliament, state legislatures, and offices of the President and Vice-President in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Part XII** of the Indian Constitution deals with finance, property, contracts, and suits. It includes provisions related to the distribution of revenue between the Union and the States.
 
• **Part IV** contains the Directive Principles of State Policy, which are guidelines for the framing of laws by the government. These principles aim to create social and economic conditions under which citizens can lead a good life.
 
• **Part XI** deals with the relations between the Union and the States, defining the distribution of legislative and administrative powers between the two.
 
• The Election Commission of India is an autonomous constitutional authority responsible for administering election processes in India at both national and state levels. The body administers elections to the Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, and State Legislative Assemblies in India, as well as the offices of the President and Vice President in the country.
 
• Being a constitutional body, the Election Commission operates independently of the government to ensure free and fair elections. Its autonomy and impartial functioning are crucial for the democratic structure of the country.

questions.question: UPSC is a Constitutional Body to conduct examinations for appointments to the services of the Union and the services of the State, respectively, under Article ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 315**__.

__
 
• Article 315 of the Indian Constitution deals with the functions of the Public Service Commissions (both Union and State).
 
• The Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) is a central recruiting agency in India responsible for appointments to and examinations for All India Services and Group A & B of Central services.
 
• The State Public Service Commissions (SPSCs) are responsible for conducting examinations for appointments to the services of the respective state governments.
 
• The duties of the UPSC and SPSCs include conducting examinations for appointments to the services, advising on the suitability of candidates for various posts, and advising on disciplinary matters affecting government employees.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Union Public Service Commission (UPSC)**

 
 
• The UPSC is an independent constitutional body established under Article 315 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It is tasked with conducting examinations for All India Services, Central Services, and public services of the centrally administered territories.
 
• The commission consists of a chairman and other members appointed by the President of India.
 
• The term of office of the members of the Commission is six years or until they attain the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier.
 
 
 
• **State Public Service Commissions (SPSCs)**
 
 
• Each state in India has its own Public Service Commission established under Article 315 to conduct examinations for appointments to the services of the state.
 
• The SPSCs advise the state government on all matters relating to recruitment, promotions, transfers, and disciplinary actions.
 
• The members of the SPSC are appointed by the Governor of the respective state.
 
• The term of office for SPSC members is also six years or until the age of 62 years, whichever is earlier.

questions.question: _______ is a set of norms and guidelines to be followed by the political parties and contesting candidates during election time.

__
 
• **Code of Conduct**__ is a set of norms and guidelines to be **followed by the political parties and contesting candidates during election time.**
 
• The **Election Commission** of India issues a set of guidelines for candidates and political parties to follow during elections.
 
• Speeches, polling booths, polling day conduct, election manifestos, processions, and general conduct are all covered under the criteria.

questions.question: The Election Commission of India was established in ________.
questions.solution:

• **The Election Commission of India **was established in **1950**.
 
• **The Election Commission of India (ECI) **is a **constitutional body **established by the **Constitution of India **with the **mandate to oversee and regulate elections **throughout the country.
 
• **Article 324** of the Constitution empowers the Election Commission with the authority and responsibility for the superintendence, direction, and control of elections to various offices, including parliament, state legislatures, the presidency, and the vice presidency.
 
• As such, the Election Commission functions as a nationwide entity, serving **both the Central government and the state governments**.
 
• This esteemed body administers elections for a multitude of governmental positions, including the Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, State Legislative Assemblies, State Legislative Councils, as well as the offices of the President and Vice President of the nation.
